caption: If your horse has been fighting collection and your trainer says his foundation is solid — believe the trainer. Something else is going on. When the mid-back seizes up, a horse physically cannot round through his topline. He'll hollow, brace, pin ears, or root the bit trying to relieve the pressure. North Texas trainers see this constantly and assume it's a fitness gap. Sometimes it is. Sometimes Dr. Leo shows up and finds three joints in the thoracic spine that haven't moved right in months. Free those up and the horse your trainer believed in finally shows up. If your horse has good training on him and still won't collect, DM us to book — we're running DFW.

One visit. Stops noticeably harder. That's not magic — that's what happens when the hips are level and the loin is free. A reining horse or rope horse that's cocked in the pelvis can't load his hindquarters evenly. He'll stop crooked, drift, or just lose power behind. Dr. Leo sees this all the time across North Texas. One adjustment, horse is square, and suddenly he's stopping like the owner always believed he could. If your horse's stops have gone flat or his slide feels off, DM us to book.

Mid-summer is when it catches up with them. Month after month of runs, hauls, and hard work — and most horses haven't had anyone check whether everything is still moving right. They compensate quietly until they can't. Dr. Leo comes to your barn across North Texas and the Great Falls area, checks the whole horse, and frees up whatever's gotten stuck. No trailering. No stress. Just a horse that feels better and works better. July slots are going fast. Book now — shortgochiro.com or call (406) 799-3369.
